text: Kanzler, it's great to have a target, but once you are in a trade you can look out for signs of a reversal and it gives you a chance to get out with some pips. The engulf north of the yellow level would have been such a sign. It indicated that price would al least retrace to your entry level. I know it is a lot easier in hindsight!

author: polymorph
text:
Hello xetrader, and welcome to RTM,

When supply exceeds demand, price falls so yes, the 2 areas you circled are supply. But If and RTM train us to move past traditional supply and demand and to understand more about what is going on. Also, a good rule of thumb is to always look left for help interpreting what's happening now. Please take a look at the pic I've marked up.

If you haven't already, take a look at the Marketpedia section. Given the questions you asked, it's probably best to start with the Supply and Demand and Caps articles (see below) and open up some charts and start marking your RBD, DBR, RBR, DBD's. Hope that helps!

Supply and Demand Caps

author: polymorph
text:
Probably best to follow in2forex's post first. Also look at the chart I've posted here. The supply and demand I marked are the 2 white lines you marked that are farthest to the left. I'd suggest zooming into the white lines you marked and then using the rectangle tool to draw a box around the areas of supply and demand and extend the zones to the right to see what price does when it meets those areas again. Does it reject price? Often it does on the first time back (FTB.) Does price blow through it? Often it does after FTB on subsequent returns. Does supply become demand/demand become supply? That often happens too (not the best example in this chart, but hopefully it illustrates the concept.)

If you should land milkeyway as a mentor, you are quite fortunate indeed because he's a superstar in the making! I don't presume to speak for him, but I think he's going to give you a clue and challenge you to dive in again and again and learn from your markings and your own mistakes. He and other RTM folks can mark these for you and say the same things about them over and over again, but you'll have to dive in and investigate for yourself to actually "get" it. As in2forex said, post, post, post your charts -if a picture (or chart) is worth 1000 words, 1000 charts are worth a million words, and someday a million dollars. Best of luck in your studies and I look forward to seeing your charts!

author: polymorph
text:
The middle section of the Supply/Demand article describes DBR/RBD/DBD/RBR's. On your charts start by focusing on the B's (the bases) in those formations and extend them out as far as they seem to matter. Regarding your yellow circles, why did you draw them there? Don't tell us, show us by using boxes on your own chart and extending them to the right to see what happens. Don't be afraid to drop to lower time frames (LTF) and refine your areas of supply and demand.

As for how wide to draw them, stop and think about what is really happening as you're doing this homework - real buying and selling is creating the picture on the chart. So in the pic I uploaded, the blue supply box is drawn around the area where buying and selling was fairly equal right before a clear decision by the market to take price lower. That's essentially what a base is: balance in price before clear imbalance, in this case price moved sideways and then selling far exceeded buying, which always means that price must fall. It also might help to think of it as decisions (If has a wholevideo on it that is phenomenal!) - where did the market make clear decisions on price? That's a base and for this homework it's what you want to mark.
